attributes.name: [OpenRouter] Cache Hit Rate Drop
attributes.description: Alerts when the request-weighted cache hit rate of a model over the last 6 hours falls below half of its own rate over the preceding days. Models that do not use prompt caching are ignored. A sudden drop can signal prompt changes, model switching, or cache invalidation that increases effective token cost.

investigation_guide.blob:
## Cache Hit Rate Drop

## How to read this alert

Kibana describes every ES|QL rule alert the same way: "Document count is 1 in the last 7d for <model>. Alert when greater than 0." It only means that the rule query returned one row for this model, so the condition was met. The alert does not show the numbers itself.

To see them, open the alert in Discover with the link in the alert details (the `kibana.alert.url` field). The query result has the values that triggered the alert: `recent_rate` (last 6 hours), `baseline_rate` (preceding days) and `recent_req` (requests in the last 6 hours).

For notifications, add a rule action and use the context variables `{{context.title}}`, `{{context.hits}}` (the result rows with those values) and `{{context.link}}` (Discover link).

Fires per model when the cache hit rate of the last 6 hours (weighted by request count) is below 50% of the same model's rate over the preceding days of the rule window (7 days). Models with a baseline below 10% (no prompt caching) and models with fewer than 20 requests in the last 6 hours are ignored.

### Triage Steps
1. Open the OpenRouter Performance dashboard and inspect the cache hit rate for the affected model.
2. Compare recent and earlier behavior:
   `FROM metrics-openrouter.performance-* | WHERE openrouter.performance.cache_hit_rate IS NOT NULL | STATS rate = SUM(openrouter.performance.cache_hit_rate * openrouter.performance.request_count) / SUM(openrouter.performance.request_count) BY openrouter.performance.model, day = BUCKET(@timestamp, 1 day)`
3. Correlate with prompt changes in your application: cache hits depend on prompt prefix stability.
4. Check whether traffic moved to a provider or key that does not cache.

### Common Causes
- Prompt prefix changes that invalidate the cache (for example dynamic system prompts with timestamps)
- A provider routing change
- Very short prompts below the minimum caching threshold

### Tuning
The constants are at the top of the query: recent period (6 hours), minimum baseline rate (0.10), minimum recent requests (20) and the fraction of the baseline (0.5). Keep the rule time window longer than the recent period so a baseline exists.
